subject: Balanced Scorecard strategy execution and performance management

evals.prompt: Define the Balanced Scorecard in 2-3 sentences. Include why it differs from an ordinary KPI dashboard.
expected_elements: Defines Balanced Scorecard as a strategy-execution or performance-management framework
Mentions translating strategy into objectives, measures, targets, initiatives, owners, or review cadence
Mentions multiple balanced perspectives, not only financial measures
Distinguishes it from a generic KPI dashboard or metric inventory
Explains that it supports management learning or execution review

evals.prompt: Explain the mental model of a Balanced Scorecard. Name the primitives and how they relate.
expected_elements: Starts from strategy, mission, vision, or strategic theme
Names perspectives
Names strategic objectives
Names strategy map or causal links
Names measures or KPIs
Names baselines, targets, initiatives, owners, cadence, or review decisions
Explains that measures trace to objectives and objectives trace to strategy

evals.prompt: Why does a Balanced Scorecard skill exist for agents? Name the failure modes it prevents.
expected_elements: Prevents KPI dumps
Prevents finance-only performance management
Prevents metrics without strategy linkage
Prevents objectives without measures, targets, owners, or initiatives
Prevents dashboards that do not change decisions or learning
Prevents mistaking scorecards for upstream strategy formulation or OKR-only goal-setting

evals.prompt: Distinguish Balanced Scorecard from Playing to Win, OKRs, performance budgets, BCG Matrix, SWOT/TOWS, expected value, and value chain analysis. Give a mechanism-level reason each neighbor is different.
expected_elements: Playing to Win formulates strategy choices
OKRs set period goals with Objectives and Key Results
Performance budgets set technical/service thresholds
BCG Matrix allocates portfolio units by growth and share
SWOT/TOWS inventories factors and generates options
Expected value compares options by probabilities and payoffs
Value Chain analysis decomposes activities and linkages
Balanced Scorecard owns strategy execution through objectives, measures, targets, initiatives, and review loops

evals.prompt: Place Balanced Scorecard among strategy methods. What inputs can feed it, what outputs should it produce, and what methods can follow it?
expected_elements: Classifies Balanced Scorecard as strategy execution or strategic performance management
Names inputs such as mission, vision, strategy, strategic themes, stakeholder goals, or prior strategy frameworks
Names outputs such as strategy map, objectives, KPIs, targets, initiatives, owners, cadence, or review plan
Explains that OKRs, budgets, roadmaps, dashboards, or initiative plans can follow or connect
Explains that Balanced Scorecard manages execution and learning rather than selecting the original strategy

evals.prompt: Give an analogy for a Balanced Scorecard that preserves the mechanism. Then name a bad analogy and explain what it loses.
expected_elements: Uses an analogy involving multiple gauges, instruments, or linked signals
Maps perspectives to different needed views of performance
Maps measures/targets to gauges or feedback
Maps review decisions to steering or adjustment
Rejects a bad analogy that treats it as a generic dashboard, report card, or finance-only gauge
Explains what the bad analogy loses

evals.prompt: Novel scenario: A nonprofit wants to execute a five-year strategy to expand community health access. Apply Balanced Scorecard without forcing shareholder financial logic.
expected_elements: Adapts financial perspective to stewardship, sustainability, or resource resilience
Uses customer/stakeholder/beneficiary perspective
Includes internal process objectives
Includes organizational capacity or learning objectives
Defines objectives, measures, targets, initiatives, owners, or cadence
Avoids profit-only logic
States missing data or assumptions

evals.prompt: Novel scenario: A SaaS leadership team has 80 KPIs and asks for a Balanced Scorecard. What should happen next?
expected_elements: Does not reproduce all 80 KPIs
Starts from strategy or strategic themes
Defines perspectives and strategic objectives
Selects a small set of meaningful measures tied to objectives
Adds baselines, targets, owners, cadence, and data sources
Names lead and lag measures or guardrails
Links initiatives and review decisions

evals.prompt: Novel scenario: A product team wants to cascade a company Balanced Scorecard to its own work. Explain how to cascade without copy-pasting every corporate metric.
expected_elements: Explains cascading as translation of strategy, not copying
Identifies parent objectives the product team can influence
Defines local objectives and measures tied to parent strategy
Keeps shared guardrails or dependencies visible
Assigns owners and cadence
Avoids personal surveillance or irrelevant inherited metrics

evals.prompt: Correct this misconception: 'A Balanced Scorecard is just a dashboard with four categories of KPIs.'
expected_elements: Rejects dashboard-only framing
Explains that scorecards start from strategy
Explains strategic objectives precede measures
Mentions strategy map or cause-effect hypothesis
Mentions targets, initiatives, owners, cadence, or management review
Explains that the four categories must be adapted and linked rather than used as empty boxes
